clue.text: Made music together?

definitions.meaning: to write a piece of music is to create it on paper
a together person is calm and collected

explanation.surface: A question about whether a group of people played or wrote music as a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Together' reads as 'in company', but here it is the informal sense of self-possessed.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music, and someone calm and unflustered is said to be collected, or together.

clue.text: African fell? Secure with rope

definitions.meaning: a North African Muslim of Berber and Arab descent
a fell is an expanse of high open upland in northern England
to tie up a boat at a quay or buoy

explanation.surface: A puzzled note about an African who took a tumble, then an instruction to tie something up.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions. 'Fell' looks like the past of 'fall' after 'African', but it is the noun for upland heath.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moors were North African people; moorland is open upland like a fell; boats are tied up at moorings.

clue.text: Mean little devil interrupts broadcaster

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the middle of the other, cutting it open

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
an imp is a small mischievous devil

explanation.surface: A nasty little rascal butts in on a radio or TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: SKY is the British satellite broadcaster; IMP breaks into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy portions are mean, meagre or stingy.

clue.text: Mostly inadequate body image?

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, so its final letter is lost

explanation.surface: A remark about poor self-esteem, a mostly negative view of one's own body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of SCANT. 'Body image' is a medical picture of the inside of the body, not self-perception.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital scan is an image of the inside of a patient's body.

clue.text: One wedding finally accepted by pair recently living in sin?

indicators.note: the outer pieces take in the inner ones, holding them inside
only the closing letter of the word wedding is used

explanation.surface: A couple who lived together unmarried finally have a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: I and G (wedding's last letter) go inside PR + OF LATE. The definition is ironic: living in sin is the old phrase for cohabiting unmarried, here stretched to mean leading a dissolute life.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate person lives a wildly dissolute, immoral life.

clue.text: Name cut from show programmed earlier

indicators.note: the named letter is removed from the word

explanation.surface: A performer's name is dropped from a show that had been scheduled in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: N, for 'name', is cut from PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A preset device or setting has been configured in advance.

clue.text: Type of jumper favoured by some equestrian team members

definitions.text: Type of jumper favoured by some equestrian team members

parts.words: Type of jumper favoured by some equestrian team members
parts.note: the jumper looks like a show-jumping horse, but it is a sweater, and the riders are players in the horseback ball game

explanation.surface: A question of which horse show-jumping teams prefer.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater; polo is a team game played on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater with a high, close-fitting, folded-over collar, named after the riders of that horseback sport.

clue.text: Put right fitting inside to toughen transport

indicators.note: the pieces are put inside the other word, so it is cut open to hold them

parts.note: to enure is to harden or accustom someone to hardship

explanation.surface: An instruction to install the right fitting to make a vehicle sturdier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like vehicles, but it is the verb: to transport someone is to delight them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away with delight, to be filled with rapture.

clue.text: Remedy after a king's injected poison

indicators.note: the letters are put into the other word, as a needle puts in a drug

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A treatment goes wrong after a monarch is given a fatal jab.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R go into CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American arrow poison that paralyses muscles.

clue.text: Sound of contentment, accepting life finally is not so bad

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a cat purrs when it is content

indicators.note: only the last letter of life is used

explanation.surface: Someone sighs happily, accepting that life in the end isn't too bad.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the last letter of 'life', goes inside PURR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more pure is cleaner and less wicked, so less bad.

clue.text: Political publication reduced to clear

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a party publishes its manifesto of policies before an election

explanation.surface: A party pamphlet is cut down to make its message plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' drops the last letter of MANIFESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest means obvious, plainly evident.

clue.text: Scientist seeing psychiatrist, so miserable

indicators.note: in a wretched state, so the letters are put in a poor, disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A scientist is so unhappy that they are in therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miserable' signals an anagram of PSYCHIATRIST plus SO.
explanation.definitionFit: One who studies the physics of stars and galaxies is a kind of scientist.

clue.text: Doesn't pen right off? But one may

definitions.text: Doesn't pen right off? But one may

indicators.note: the letters go off, gone bad, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't write back at once, set against one who does.
explanation.walkthrough: An anagram, signalled by 'off', of DOESNT, PEN and R. The whole clue also defines: one who answers does pen a reply right off.
explanation.definitionFit: A respondent is one who replies, so is the person who would write back promptly.

clue.text: Beyond words, exceptionally fine fiction

indicators.note: in an unusual way, so the letters are taken out of their usual order

parts.note: a fable is a made-up story

explanation.surface: Praise for a novel so exceptional that it cannot be described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' scrambles FINE into INEF, then FABLE is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too great to be expressed in speech is ineffable.

clue.text: Debate's inconclusive, in the event

indicators.note: without a conclusion, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to debate is to discuss; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A discussion fails to reach a conclusion during the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: DISCUSS loses its final letter. 'The event' is an athletics field event.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the heavy disc is an athletics field event.

clue.text: Rule out movement lacking wind and notes

parts.note: B and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: An instruction ruling out a musical movement for wind instruments and notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' looks musical, beside 'wind' and 'notes', but it means motion; a sailing ship with no wind is stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: To becalm a ship is to leave it unable to move for lack of wind.

clue.text: For such a poet, doom isn't unusual

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so the letters are out of their ordinary order

explanation.surface: A remark that gloomy themes are normal for a certain kind of poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' signals an anagram of DOOM and ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A monody is a mournful elegy for one voice, and its writer is a poet of laments.

clue.text: Push drink before girl that's game in pub?

indicators.note: the drink comes ahead of the girl in the answer

parts.note: a half is a half-pint of beer

explanation.surface: Someone pushes a drink towards a girl, which is the done thing in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Shove-ha'penny is a British pub game of sliding coins up a board; a half is a half-pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British pub game in which coins are pushed along a marked board.

clue.text: Exercises, running up and down pitch?

definitions.text: Exercises, running up and down pitch?

parts.words: Exercises, running up and down pitch?
parts.note: the picture is athletes training up and down a sports field, but the pitch is musical, and the exercises are a musician's practice

explanation.surface: Athletes doing training laps up and down a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a football field; it is the height of a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians practise series of notes rising and falling in pitch.

clue.text: Mount a second colt before finish

indicators.note: these pieces come ahead of the finish in the answer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for colt in horse-racing form

explanation.surface: A rider mounts a second young horse before the race ends.
explanation.walkthrough: C for colt is a racing-card abbreviation. 'Mount' looks like a horse; it is the verb to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount stairs or a hill is to climb up it.

clue.text: Scoffing 50 per cent of tinned fish, mostly kept in reserve

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the first four of its eight letters

parts.note: sardines are often sold in tins

indicators.note: most of the phrase, losing its last letter

parts.note: something on ice is held in readiness for later

explanation.surface: Someone eats half a tin of sardines, keeping the rest stored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffing' looks like eating greedily; it is mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardonic remark is mocking and contemptuous.

clue.text: Expected behaviour for little boy

indicators.note: a shortened form, as a pet name is a short version of the full name

explanation.surface: A rule of conduct for a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' cuts NORMAN to its short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard pattern of conduct, what is usual.

clue.text: Submitted front section to editor

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A journalist sent the opening part of an article to the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submitted' looks like sending in copy; it means yielded.
explanation.definitionFit: To bow to someone's will is to give in, yield.

clue.text: Very small part one gets in week of festival

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, as in not a jot

definitions.text: one gets in week of festival
definitions.meaning: a word that goes in front of week to name the week of the Whitsun festival

explanation.surface: A tiny portion that someone receives during a festival week.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a fill-in: the word one puts with 'week' to name the week of Whitsun, the Christian festival of Pentecost.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a jot means not the tiniest bit; Whitsun week is the week of Pentecost.

clue.text: One inclined to be less yielding

definitions.meaning: someone or something that tilts or rests at a slant
producing less, as a poor year or harvest gives a smaller crop

explanation.surface: A person disposed to be more stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less yielding' looks like 'more stubborn', but it means less productive, as in lean years.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that leans is tilted; lean times are thin and unproductive.

clue.text: Most wanting resolution to see it end

indicators.note: a working out, so the letters are re-solved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone eager to settle a matter and see it finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolution' signals an anagram of SEE IT END.
explanation.definitionFit: The neediest people are the poorest, lacking most.
